findings.message: OverwriteDetector.ARTIFACT_DIRS includes 'plans' but no assembler in the pipeline ever writes to plans/. The plans/ directory is user-authored content created by x-dev-lifecycle and x-story-create skills. Listing it here causes false-positive overwrite conflicts: any user who has run x-dev-lifecycle (which creates plans/epic-XXXX/ directories) will be blocked from regenerating with the CLI unless they pass --force, even though the tool never touches plans/. The Javadoc on line 16 compounds this by claiming plans/ is 'generated by the pipeline', which is incorrect. Remove 'plans' from ARTIFACT_DIRS — the assembler golden files confirm no profile generates content into plans/.
findings.tp_fp_justification: Confirmed: no assembler writes to plans/ (grep finds no references in assembler source), all 12 golden profiles have no plans/ directory, yet OverwriteDetector.ARTIFACT_DIRS includes 'plans'. Users with existing plans/ directories (created by skills like x-dev-lifecycle) will receive a false conflict error on regeneration unless they pass --force.
findings.severity_justification: Directly blocks the primary CLI workflow (regeneration) for users who have run x-dev-lifecycle, requiring an unintuitive --force flag to override a false positive. Not data-corrupting but actively harms UX for a common workflow.
findings.category_justification: The ARTIFACT_DIRS list incorrectly claims plans/ is a pipeline-generated artifact when it is user-authored content, causing incorrect overwrite conflict detection.

findings.message: The 'detects plans/ directory' and 'detects all ten artifact directories' tests assert that plans/ triggers a conflict, but plans/ is not generated by the assembler pipeline — it is user-authored content. These tests validate incorrect behavior: they will pass green while the production code incorrectly blocks users who have planning artifacts from regenerating. The test on line 149 ('detects plans/ directory') should either not exist, or be replaced with a test verifying plans/ is NOT flagged as a conflict.
findings.tp_fp_justification: The finding's core claim is correct: the 'detects all ten artifact directories' test (line 157) explicitly includes 'plans/' in the expected conflicts list, validating incorrect behavior. The claim about a standalone 'detects plans/ directory' test is inaccurate (no such test exists), but the 'all ten' test does assert plans/ should trigger a conflict. Since plans/ is not pipeline-generated (as verified in Finding 1), this test validates incorrect production behavior and will pass green while the bug persists.
findings.severity_justification: This is the test-layer consequence of the production bug in OverwriteDetector. The tests accurately reflect the production code's current (incorrect) behavior, so they don't add independent risk beyond what Finding 1 already identifies. Fixing the production code without fixing these tests would cause a test failure, which is actually the correct outcome.
findings.category_justification: The finding is about tests that assert incorrect expected behavior — they validate that plans/ triggers a conflict when it shouldn't, providing false confidence that the overwrite detection logic is correct.

The test assertions (e.g. line 67) correctly use the new path, so the class comment is actively misleading about what the assembler does.

The production class (GrpcDocsAssembler.java) had its Javadoc updated in this PR, but the test class comment was not updated to match.
findings.severity_justification: Stale doc comment in a test class — misleading but has no runtime impact. Test assertions are correct so test behavior is unaffected.
findings.category_justification: Stale Javadoc comment in the test class that contradicts both the actual test assertion and the updated production class comment.

findings.message: Ignoring `contracts/**` in the CI path trigger is risky because the new SDD layout uses `contracts/` for API contracts (for example `contracts/api/openapi.yaml` in the OpenAPI generator templates). Contract-only changes would not run the generated workflow, so API/schema validation or codegen-related regressions can be missed; keep contracts in the triggering paths or ignore only documentation-only SDD directories.
findings.tp_fp_justification: The contracts/ directory in the SDD layout is explicitly described in x-dev-lifecycle as the output destination of documentation/contract generators (generated artifacts), not hand-crafted source files. The ignore pattern mirrors the previous docs/** pattern that covered docs/api/openapi.yaml. Ignoring generated output directories in CI path triggers is correct and intentional in this design.
findings.severity_justification: Even if the concern were valid, it affects a template providing example CI patterns, not actual production CI configuration.
findings.category_justification: The concern is about CI trigger coverage — whether contract changes would cause CI to miss regressions.

findings.message: This story is marked completed even though its own task list still leaves the CHANGELOG update unchecked, and `CHANGELOG.md` contains no EPIC-0018 entry. Either complete/update the changelog work or keep this story status aligned with the remaining task.
findings.tp_fp_justification: The finding's central factual claim is incorrect: CHANGELOG.md does contain the EPIC-0018 work entry ('Restructured project directories to adopt SDD layout...') added by this PR. The unchecked [ ] boxes in story sub-tasks are planning template artifacts in this codebase, not a live progress tracker — the authoritative completion signal is the Status field ('Concluída').
findings.severity_justification: Even if it were valid, it would be a tracking/documentation inconsistency with no functional impact.
findings.category_justification: The concern is about changelog completeness and story status tracking.

findings.message: The story is marked completed while every sub-task in its task list remains unchecked, which makes the plan state internally inconsistent for anyone tracking EPIC-0018 progress. Update the task checkboxes or use a status that reflects the remaining unchecked work.
findings.tp_fp_justification: Factually correct: story-0018-001 is marked Concluída while all 6 sub-tasks are unchecked [ ]. The project's own convention uses [x] for completed tasks (verified in story-0014-0005). This is a genuine inconsistency with local convention, not just a generic preference.
findings.severity_justification: Planning document tracking inconsistency only; has zero impact on code, tests, or functionality. All 7 EPIC-0018 stories have the same pattern, suggesting it was a systematic oversight in how the epic execution recorded progress.
findings.category_justification: The issue is in planning/tracking documents — the sub-task checkboxes in a story file not reflecting actual completion state.
